title: Sortase A ΔN59: P94 chemistry and β7–β8 loop coupling
objective: Distinguish P94 side-chain chemistry, Y187 loop packing and functional coupling using eight soluble S. aureus ΔN59 constructs. All literature evidence was published before 2026-01-01.
coordinate_note: Construct coordinates include the 17-aa His6–TEV tag/scar prefix. Native full-length SrtA numbering = precursor position + 42 in the native segment. ΔN59 is Q60–K206, 147 aa. Expression precursor 164 aa; after TEV, one Gly scar plus the domain gives 148 aa. All mutation names use native full-length numbering.

hypotheses.question: Does the gain require arginine at P94, or can neutral replacements reproduce it?
hypotheses.mechanism: Removing the proline ring can alter the H1 backbone or packing, while Arg can add distinct electrostatic interactions. Compare Arg with two neutral replacements without assuming that chemistry is isolated perfectly.
hypotheses.measurement: WT versus P94R, P94S and P94A: initial LC–MS ligation rates across donor and GGG concentrations; LPETG versus LPATG. Similar neutral-mutant gains argue that Arg is unnecessary; a donor-dependent Arg advantage suggests substrate-specific effects.
hypotheses.note: This focused chemical comparison is not a complete saturation scan and cannot separate backbone freedom from side-chain packing by itself.

hypotheses.question: Does Y187 aromatic packing or its hydroxyl group influence the loop contribution?
hypotheses.mechanism: Y187L removes aromaticity and the phenol while retaining a hydrophobic side chain. Y187F retains aromaticity but removes the hydroxyl. These distinguish two components of a possible H1–loop packing interaction.
hypotheses.measurement: Compare Y187L, Y187F and WT for ligation kinetics, soluble monomer fraction and local NMR/HDX changes. A larger L than F effect supports aromatic packing, conditional on preserved folding.
hypotheses.note: The single Y187L effect is exploratory on the WT background; published benefits involved E189 substitutions and 5M.

hypotheses.question: Is the P94R effect dependent on the identity of Y187?
hypotheses.mechanism: The WT/P94R/Y187L/P94R–Y187L factorial tests whether perturbing the H1 position and the facing loop residue gives independent functional effects.
hypotheses.measurement: Fit a log-scale interaction term to a matched kinetic parameter: log[(eta_RL * eta_WT)/(eta_R * eta_L)], eta = kcat/KM,donor at demonstrated saturating GGG. Bootstrap uncertainty across independent preparations. Repeat for kcat and GGG dependence, and map loop dynamics in the four constructs.
hypotheses.note: Nonadditivity establishes functional coupling under the measured conditions; it does not alone prove direct contact or an open-state stabilization mechanism.

hypotheses.question: How much apparent product formation survives removal of the catalytic nucleophile?
hypotheses.mechanism: C184A removes the cysteine required to form the acyl-enzyme intermediate.
hypotheses.measurement: C184A, WT and no-enzyme mixtures in the same LC–MS assay; use the inactive mutant to identify enzyme-preparation background rather than fitting kinetics to it.

variants.name: WT ΔN59
variants.headline: Wild-type catalytic domain
variants.note: Complete expression precursor: M–His6–GSS–ENLYFQ|G–Q60…K206. Cleave and remove the tag before mechanistic assays; the mature enzyme is G–Q60…K206 (148 aa). rationale.hypothesis: Arg provides a distinct route to changing the P94-containing cleft wall.

observations.finding: P94S and P94R were enriched during evolution; individual P94S analysis showed altered donor kinetics and a penalty in GGG recognition.
observations.locator: Directed evolution Results, Fig. 3, discussion following Table 1
observations.context: S. aureus soluble sortase; yeast selection followed by purified-enzyme HPLC kinetics with LPETG and GGG substrates.

rationale.comparison: WT, P94S and P94A; also the P94R/Y187L factorial. Measure donor and GGG saturation, product partitioning and LPETG/LPATG dependence.
rationale.uncertainty: The evolved 5M benefit does not establish a single-P94R fold improvement in this tag-cleaved background. An LPETG-specific advantage could reflect substrate chemistry rather than loop opening.
rationale.edit: Introduces a positively charged side chain at the cleft wall.
rationale.inference: If P94R alone outperforms neutral substitutions only on LPETG, test substrate-specific electrostatic recognition before assigning loop-mediated activation.

rationale.hypothesis: A neutral polar replacement tests whether arginine is required for the gain.

rationale.comparison: P94R versus P94S versus WT at matched substrate and active-enzyme concentrations.
rationale.uncertainty: Ser changes side-chain size, hydrogen-bonding and backbone constraints together; a result is a chemical comparison rather than a pure charge intervention.
rationale.edit: Uses a neutral polar residue as a published alternative to arginine.
rationale.inference: A gain with Ser rules out a strict requirement for an Arg side chain, but does not establish which conformational feature changed.

rationale.hypothesis: A small neutral nonpolar replacement asks whether removal of proline is sufficient to change activity.

observations.finding: P94 lies in the short helix that forms a lateral wall of the active-site cleft.

rationale.comparison: P94A against WT and P94S, with P94R as the charged comparison.
rationale.uncertainty: Ala changes local packing and helix propensity as well as removing the proline ring; shared gains would be consistent with, but would not prove, a backbone mechanism.
rationale.edit: Removes the cyclic side chain without adding polarity or charge.
rationale.inference: This is an exploratory chemical control derived from pre-2026 structure, without claiming a pre-2026 measured P94A gain.

rationale.hypothesis: Removing Y187 aromaticity may change packing between the loop and H1.

observations.finding: Y187L/E189R and Y187L/E189A improved activity on an already evolved 5M background; neither comparison isolates Y187L alone.
observations.context: S. aureus evolved 5M plus loop substitutions; protein ligation FRET and peptide HPLC assays.

observations.finding: Sorting-signal analog attachment displaced the β7–β8 loop away from H1 and exposed a groove mapped by Gly3-dependent NMR chemical shifts.

observations.context: S. aureus ΔN59, calcium-containing NMR samples; covalent Cbz-LPAT* intermediate mimic, not a freely exchanging Michaelis complex.

rationale.comparison: Y187L versus WT and Y187F; local structural readout plus LC–MS kinetics.
rationale.uncertainty: Published Y187L benefits are confounded with E189 and evolved-background substitutions; Leu may destabilize or repack the loop rather than favor productive access.
rationale.edit: Removes the aromatic ring while retaining a hydrophobic side chain.
rationale.inference: This isolates one component of a published successful combination; its behavior on WT is not established by that combination.

rationale.hypothesis: Retaining the aromatic ring while removing its hydroxyl distinguishes phenol chemistry from aromatic packing.

rationale.comparison: Y187F versus Y187L and WT; compare kinetic changes and folding.
rationale.uncertainty: Phe can still change rotamers and loop packing; it is not an exact structural rescue of Tyr.
rationale.edit: Retains an aromatic side chain while removing the phenolic hydroxyl.
rationale.inference: A near-WT Phe phenotype with an altered Leu phenotype supports an aromatic contribution, provided both proteins remain folded.

rationale.hypothesis: The effect of P94R may depend on the facing loop residue.

rationale.comparison: Complete WT/P94R/Y187L/double matrix; compare kinetic interaction terms and loop NMR or HDX signals under identical ligand states.
rationale.uncertainty: Kinetic nonadditivity can arise from a change in the rate-limiting step or folding. It is not a direct-contact free energy, and a null interaction does not exclude coupling through other loop residues.
rationale.edit: Adds the P94 substitution to the isolated loop mutant to complete the factorial comparison.
rationale.inference: Submultiplicative effects are compatible with a shared mechanism; supermultiplicative effects imply cooperation or a new interaction. Local dynamics evidence is needed to assign loop-state changes.

rationale.hypothesis: Product formation should require the catalytic cysteine.

observations.finding: C184 is the active-site nucleophile; the paper cites loss of activity with C184A.
observations.context: S. aureus soluble ΔN59 structural and biochemical context.

rationale.comparison: C184A versus WT and a no-enzyme blank; assay ligation and hydrolysis products separately.
rationale.uncertainty: C184A is not an inactive structural mimic of the thioacyl intermediate and should not be used as a substrate-binding surrogate.
rationale.inference: Product in the inactive preparation indicates background or contamination requiring resolution before assigning mechanistic gains.

tracks.label: Conservation in the SrtA UniRef50 cluster

scale.higher_means: more conserved across this comparison set

method.comparison_set: UniProtKB members of UniRef50_Q2FV99, the UniRef50 cluster containing Q9S446: the same protein in other species, clustered by UniProt at 50% identity with an 80% length-overlap requirement. ORTHOLOG level: scores answer what this protein needs.
method.alignment: multiple alignment by FAMSA via pyfamsa 0.7.0, projected onto reference coordinates by dropping columns where the reference is gapped. It can score positions that MAFFT leaves unscored, with weak support, so read per-position coverage alongside the score
method.weighting: Henikoff position-based sequence weights, computed over variable columns only
method.effective_sequences_definition: Neff = sum(1/n_i), n_i counting sequences at least 80% identical to sequence i over positions where both have a residue (itself included); pairs overlapping less than 50% of the reference are not counted as similar. Reported unnormalised and divided by reference length; normalisation is not standardised in the literature, so compare only against values computed the same way. This is NOT the sum of the Henikoff weights, which is rescaled to the sequence count by construction and therefore always equals it.
method.score: Jensen-Shannon divergence against Robinson & Robinson background, scaled by column occupancy (Capra & Singh 2007)
method.projection: Full native Q9S446 positions 60–206 mapped without substitutions to precursor positions 18–164. All 17 synthetic tag/scar positions are unscored; 147/147 native catalytic-domain positions scored.
method.selection_caveat: UniRef50 membership is a homology cluster, not a phylogenetic proof of one-to-one orthology. A contemporary sequence snapshot was used, separately from the literature cutoff.

precedent_search.scope: Primary-literature search completed before construct selection: foundational structures and evolution; forward literature through 2025 for P94, Y187, β7–β8 loop, donor/amine recognition, engineered sortases and loop grafts. 2016, 2021 and 2024 primary follow-up studies inspected. Search returned later P94 studies dated 2026; those were excluded from evidence and no outcome from them is used.
